10.1002_adfm.77182: The practical application of zinc metal batteries remains severely impeded by dendritic growth at the electrolyte/electrode interface. A self‐amplifying vicious cycle involving ion depletion and localized electric‐field distortion exacerbates interfacial charge accumulation, leading to the formation of dendrites. This work designs a Lewis acid polymer electrolyte to rectify Zn 2+ transport for disrupting this detrimental cycle. Within this framework, the unsaturated Ti (Lewis acidic) sites on Ti 3 C 2 T x ‐NH 2 ‐O v anchor anions, effectively sieving ions for unrestricted Zn 2+ conduction. Meanwhile, Ti 3 C 2 T x ‐NH 2 ‐O v nanosheets restrict the conformational freedom of the polymer chains (carboxymethyl cellulose and poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate), while amino functionalization establishes balanced coordination sites within the polymer matrix, collectively constructing well‐aligned Zn 2+ transport channels. This synergistic regulation rectifies Zn 2+ flux, enabling the electrolyte to achieve an ultrahigh Zn 2+ transference number of 0.88 and high ionic conductivity of 6.8 mS cm −1 , even under ultralow liquid content (0.1 µL mg −1 ). The continuous and directional supply of Zn 2+ alleviates local charge accumulation. Zn//Zn cells demonstrate remarkably stable cycling for over 5000 h. Furthermore, full batteries coupled with high mass loading vanadium‐ and iodine‐based cathodes exhibit superior cycling durability. This work provides a novel pathway toward dendrite‐free metal batteries by tailoring ion‐transport features to resolve interfacial failure.
10.1016_j.enceco.2026.04.012: Oyster gills function as a filter-feeding organ and the first line of immune defense, constituting a primary site for microplastic interaction and toxicity. However, tissue heterogeneity of oyster gills obscures the immunotoxicity induced by micro- and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs). Here, we reported the toxicity of MPs and NPs on bivalve gills at the single-cell level. This study indicated that at comparable particle concentration (200 μg/L), NPs displayed higher accumulation potential than MPs, with distinct histopathology induced by MPs and NPs. scRNA-seq analysis revealed that NPs specifically targeted prohemocytes (PHCs), reducing their population by 47.0% and disrupting their differentiation trajectory. In contrast, MPs significantly reduced epithelial cell numbers and disrupted the temporal dynamics of subtype differentiation. NPs dysregulated the SEMA6-PLXNA neuroimmune pathway, altering the role of PHCs from signal senders to receivers, which subsequently activated the autophagy and inhibited the CD45 immune checkpoint. MPs triggered compensatory proliferation of macrophage-like cells (MLCs) via the CADM pathway. Pseudotime analysis further revealed that NPs disrupted the dynamic expression of ribosomal genes, thereby blocking the differentiation trajectory of PHCs, MLCs, and GCs. This study provides the first immune-cell atlas of bivalve gills and proposes a differentiation-blockade index coupled with a dual biomarker system (neural-cell stability/PHC loss rate) for diagnosing MNPs toxicity.
